title: Saying I Don't Know Without Losing Credibility
meta: B2 · 约 280 词 · 场景：回答问题

sections.heading: 1. Two Engineers, One Question
paragraphs: Imagine two engineers being asked the same thing in a review.
"How many users will this migration affect?"
The first one answers right away with a confident number.
The second says, "I don't know yet, but I can find out by tomorrow."
A week later, the first number turns out to be wrong by a factor of ten.
From then on, people quietly double-check everything that engineer says.
The second engineer, meanwhile, has become the person whose answers people __take at face value__.
**Credibility does not come from always knowing; it comes from being right about what you know.**
Leaders learn very quickly whose ==confidence== is ==calibrated== and whose is just a performance.
A ==bluff== might save you for one meeting, but it costs you the next ten.
sections.heading_zh: 1. 两个工程师，同一个问题
paragraphs_zh: 想象两个工程师在评审会上被问了同一个问题。
「这次迁移会影响多少用户？」
第一个张口就给了一个很自信的数字。
第二个说：「我现在还不知道，但明天之前能查清楚。」
一周后，第一个数字被发现差了十倍。
从那以后，那个工程师说的每句话，大家都会悄悄再核实一遍。
而第二个工程师，成了那个说什么大家都直接信的人。
信誉不是来自什么都知道，而是来自你对自己知道的东西判断准确。
领导很快就能看出来，谁的自信是有分寸的，谁的只是在表演。
硬撑也许能帮你混过一个会，但接下来十个会都要还。

sections.heading: 2. Make Not Knowing Sound Useful
paragraphs: The trick is to never stop at "I don't know."
**Follow it with what you do know, how you will find out, and when.**
"I don't have the exact number, but it's only users on the old app version, and I'll pull the figure from the logs by noon."
It also helps to __put a number on your certainty__.
"I'm fairly sure it's under ten percent, maybe seventy percent ==confident==."
This sounds ==precise== even when the answer is rough, and it tells people how much weight to give it.
If the question is outside your area, __point to the right person__ instead of guessing.
"That's really a question for the data team, I'll ==loop in== Anna."
Finally, close the gap you opened.
Send the real answer when you promised, even if nobody reminds you.
Each time you do this, the words "I don't know" become a little more ==trustworthy==.
sections.heading_zh: 2. 让「不知道」听起来也有用
paragraphs_zh: 诀窍是永远别停在「我不知道」上。
后面要接上你知道什么、你打算怎么查、什么时候给答复。
「具体数字我手上没有，但只涉及老版本 app 的用户，中午前我从日志里把数拉出来。」
给你的把握程度报个数也很有帮助。
「我比较确定在百分之十以下，大概七成把握。」
哪怕答案很粗略，这样说听起来也很精确，还能让大家知道这个答案该信几分。
如果问题超出了你的范围，就指给对的人，别瞎猜。
「这个其实得问数据团队，我把 Anna 拉进来。」
最后，把你留下的口子补上。
在你承诺的时间把真实答案发出去，哪怕没人提醒你。
每这样做一次，你说「我不知道」时就更值得信任一点。

gist.q: 两位工程师的例子说明了什么？
gist.a: 随口给出错误数字的人从此被人怀疑；坦诚说“不知道但明天给你”的人反而赢得信任。

gist.q: 作者认为可信度从哪里来？
gist.a: 不是永远都知道答案，而是对自己知道的部分判断准确，信心与实际相符。

gist.q: 说“不知道”之后应该补充什么？
gist.a: 说出已知部分、怎么查、什么时候给答案；给出把握程度；不是自己领域就指向对的人；按时兑现承诺。

prompts.q: 评审会上，总监问你：“这次数据库迁移会让多少请求变慢？”你没有确切数字。用 30 秒回答：说已知部分、把握程度、怎么查、什么时候给结果。
prompts.ref: I don't have an exact number yet. What I do know is that only the reporting queries touch the old tables, and those are a small share of our traffic. My best guess is under five percent of requests, and I'd say I'm about seventy percent confident in that. I'll run a replay test this afternoon and send you the real figure by tomorrow morning.
prompts.ref_zh: 我现在还没有确切的数字。我知道的是，只有报表查询会碰到老表，而这部分只占我们流量的一小块。我最好的估计是不到百分之五的请求，大概有七成把握。今天下午我跑一个回放测试，明早之前把准确数字发给你。

prompts.q: 客户沟通会上，有人问你一个法务合规的问题，不在你的领域。用 30 秒不丢面子地说不知道，并指向对的人。
prompts.ref: That's a great question, and I don't want to give you a half-right answer on something this important. Data retention rules are really owned by our legal and privacy team. What I can tell you is that the system supports deleting user data on request. I'll loop in our privacy lead today, and we'll come back to you with a written answer this week.
prompts.ref_zh: 这个问题很好，这么重要的事，我不想给你一个半对不对的答案。数据保留的规则其实归法务和隐私团队管。我能告诉你的是，系统支持按用户请求删除数据。我今天就把隐私负责人拉进来，这周内给你一个书面答复。

words.ex: We have high confidence in the fix, but we'll keep monitoring.

words.zh: （判断）校准过的、与实际相符的
words.ex: His estimates are well calibrated; when he says two weeks, it's two weeks.
The confident answer was a bluff, and the logs proved it.
I'm confident the cache is warm before peak hours.
Can you be more precise about when the errors started?
Let me loop in the security team before we open the port.
These metrics aren't trustworthy until we fix the double counting.
Don't take the vendor's benchmark at face value.
We can't say with certainty that the patch fixed it.
